briefing.headline: OpenAI o4 and xAI Grok-3 push multi-agent frontiers as US-China compute race intensifies

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: Frontier labs released nine major models this month with OpenAI and xAI leading multi-agent benchmarks. Funding hit $9.8B this quarter driven by infrastructure deals. Prompt injection and supply-chain risks remain top operational concerns.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI shipped o4-preview with 40% gains on agentic tasks while xAI launched Grok-3 trained on 100k H100s. DeepSeek-V3 and Meta's Llama-4 variants closed the gap on reasoning suites.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems and that DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level. New NIST guidelines target agent-to-agent authentication.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: TSMC Arizona fabs ramped 3nm AI chips for Google and Microsoft. CoreWeave closed $2.1B round for 100k GPU cluster expansion.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will multi-agent protocol standards emerge before state actors weaponize autonomous swarms?
